craft_claim: Carnivalesque irreverence works by temporarily dragging the lofty down into material, bodily, or mundane terms for the duration of a sanctioned frame, after which ordinary hierarchy resumes.

supporting_evidence.location: p. 10 carnival framing paragraph (pagination verified via peer-reviewed citations; chapter-level locators unverified)
supporting_evidence.note: The carnival frame is described as a temporary inversion with defined duration and place — the lofty is brought down while the festival lasts, then restored.

supporting_evidence.location: Composite text via Project Gutenberg ebook #1200; analysis rests on Bakhtin's reading, chapter locators unverified
supporting_evidence.note: The giant-body comic mode punctures knightly, clerical, and scholastic pomp through appetite and excess — debasement of the elevated to the physical, per the Bakhtin-mediated reading (work analysis_status: partial).

counterevidence.note: Locator limits are material: only the p. 10 paragraph was verified, and no source in this silo documents the scholarly debate over Bakhtin's singular reading of Rabelais — that reception question is recorded as evidence-incomplete rather than asserted either way.

scope: Festival- and parody-framed prose that invokes a recognized carnival license (comic anarchy, bodily deflation of dignitaries); chiefly long-form comic fiction and festive satire-adjacent narration.
exceptions: Outside a legible carnival license, bodily deflation of a real individual reads as insult, not carnival.
The mechanism explains the moment of debasement; it does not by itself supply the work's critique (that would be satirical-literature's engine).
